newsitem.title: USA: California backs quake victims in claims dispute.
newsitem.headline: California backs quake victims in claims dispute.

text.p: California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said on Monday that insurance companies should pay the late claims of hundreds of homeowners hit by the 1994 Northridge earthquake.
In a legal opinion by the state Department of Insurance, Quackenbush called for the companies to pay the claims even though the damages were discovered long after the earthquake.
Quackenbush said the opinion would help bring to a close at least 450 late insurance claim cases stemming from the Northridge earthquake.
The 1994 Northridge earthquake, which had a 6.8-magnitude, killed more than 50 people and caused billions of dollars in damage throughout the Los Angeles area.

The Department of Insurance said it continues to receive complaints from Northridge earthquake victims who were denied claims for damages discovered one year after the earthquake or after an earlier claim had been submitted.

"To help consumers bring these claims to closure, I believe it is important to express my legal opinion on this issue in the hope that outstanding claims, many of which are in litigation, can now be settled promptly," Quackenbush said.
